text:
sam: quick share — did a quant sensitivity sweep for llama-v2-13b bring-up across regions (us-west1 / eu-west1 / ap-southeast1) on H100 and A100. putting raw numbers + notes below, tl;dr at the top.

sam: TL;DR: H100 FP8 gives best latency/throughput balance with <0.5% QA-F1 delta vs fp16 in our eval set; A100 INT8 gives highest tokens/s but larger quality regressions and p99 tail at scale. region networking impacts throughput for batching (ap-southeast1 slightly worse for large-batch streaming).

mia: can you paste the perf table? also which kernels did you run?

sam: ran two kernel stacks: 1) triton-fast (our optimized continuous-batching path + fused attention kernels) 2) flash-attn-v2 fallback (kernel compatibility). tests used same prompt mix (70% chat, 30% long-form generation), batcher target latency 150ms. eval set: 2k QA pairs + 1k summarization samples.

sam: raw CSV (columns: model,region,gpu,quant,kernel,throughput_tok_s,p99_ms,median_ms,qa_f1_delta):
```
model,region,gpu,quant,kernel,throughput_tok_s,p99_ms,median_ms,qa_f1_delta
llama-v2-13b,us-west1,H100,fp16,triton-fast,9400,18,7,0.0
llama-v2-13b,us-west1,H100,fp8,triton-fast,11200,22,8, -0.3
llama-v2-13b,us-west1,H100,int8,flash-attn,12800,40,12, -1.1
llama-v2-13b,eu-west1,A100,fp16,triton-fast,7600,24,10,0.0
llama-v2-13b,eu-west1,A100,fp8,triton-fast,9150,30,11, -0.6
llama-v2-13b,ap-southeast1,H100,fp8,triton-fast,9800,28,10, -0.4
llama-v2-13b,ap-southeast1,A100,int8,flash-attn,12300,46,15, -1.3
```

arjun: interesting that A100 INT8 throughput beats H100 FP8 in tokens/s. what's the sequence-length distribution? maybe A100 better for short sequences?

sam: good call — workload was 70% <=256 tokens, 30% 512-1024. INT8 wins for short sequences due to denser GEMM kernel utilization, but p99 suffers because KV cache handling on the int8 codepath isn't as optimized yet.

jen: any quality regressions on summarization (ROUGE/L) beyond QA-F1?

sam: summarization ROUGE-L delta: FP8 ~ -0.25 pts, INT8 ~ -0.9 pts. Perplexity on eval set: fp16 baseline 12.4, fp8 12.9 (+4%), int8 14.1 (+13%).

perf-bot: CI report: https://internal.redwood/ci/quant-sweep/1780012345 (includes full traces and per-socket breakdown) :thumbsup:

arjun: kernel notes? any cuBLAS vs custom kernels?

sam: triton-fast uses our fused-attn + custom KV layout + selective fp32 accumulation for stability. flash-attn fallback uses vendor kernels (good for compatibility). On H100 we saw kernel-level speedup when enabling sm90-optimized kernels (small env var flip), ~8-10% throughput. On A100 int8 used custom packing that increases GEMM efficiency but increases memory traffic causing tail latency.

mia: capacity sizing ask — for 99th p99 <= 25ms what do you recommend per region?

sam: rough guidance for our request mix (avg 512 tokens):
- H100 FP16/triton-fast: ~1600 concurrent RPS per GPU to stay p99<25ms (approx 9k tokens/s sustained).
- H100 FP8/triton-fast: ~1900 RPS per GPU (11k tok/s) but keep probe rollout + canary — slight quality delta.
- A100 INT8/flash-attn: ~2100 RPS per GPU (12.5k tok/s) for median, but to keep p99<25ms you'd need ~1.4x capacity due to tails.

sam: recommendation: default to H100 FP16 for initial canary, promote FP8 with triton-fast after quality checks. Only use A100 INT8 for batch-heavy, throughput-first customers where small QA regressions are acceptable.

jen: add an eval/regression alert if QA-F1 drops >0.5 or ROUGE-L >0.5 — we should block automated rollouts.

sam: agreed — I'll add alert thresholds and add the long-form eval set to canary runs.

perf-bot: note: ap-southeast1 network egress increased variance; consider regional cache warmup + smaller initial batch sizes in APAC.

arjun: action items?

sam: 1) add fp8 canary job to rollout pipeline (probing on us-west1 + eu-west1) — assigned sam
2) hook QA-F1/ROUGE-L thresholds into rollout guard — assigned jen
3) follow-up perf run with 90/10 long-form/short-form mix and kernel-level tracing — assigned arjun
4) publish short note in eng-ml channel summarizing capacity guidance — assigned mia

mia: will draft the thread summary and post dashboard snapshots. thanks all. :rocket:
